caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001535
attempts.paper_title: Sampling representational plasticity of simple imagined movements across days enables long-term neuroprosthetic control
attempts.entry_title: Long-term ECoG BCI training trials of participant B1 (Natraj et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Almost none of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, and none was contradicted. The dandiset holds only participant B1's decoder training trials, so the somatotopy of imagined movements, the closed-loop gains in accuracy and class separation, stable plug-and-play control over weeks and the robot arm results lack the second participant, band-power features or online decoder outputs. The one claim that held, the amount of training data (837.4 min stored), depends on counting the robot trials. Without them the total is 540.0 min. A spatial pooling control could not be tested either, as no electrodes table places the channels.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Natraj, Seko, Abiri, Miao, Yan, Graham, Tu-Chan, Chang and Ganguly (2025) that can be tested on dandiset 001535, which holds the 9737 trials of high-gamma and low-frequency features that participant B1's biLSTM decoder was trained on. Only the amount of training data can be tested; the other findings need participant B3, the Figure 1 task, the band-power features of the MLP decoders, session and context labels, online decoder outputs or robot kinematics, none of which the dandiset holds.

outcomes.statement: In B1, the daily manifolds of ReFit-KF velocity commands are much less stable across days than those of discrete actions; most day pairs (65%) share no similar layer, feedforward commands never do, and commands within 45 degrees share 1.5 layers on average.
outcomes.source: Figure S7C-D legend; Results, Stability of action representations, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Specifically, the majority of the pairwise comparisons (65%, averaged for both types of commands) between individual days’ autoencoders had no significantly similar layers between them

statistics.about: discrete against within 45 degrees, layer CKA
feedforward against within 45 degrees, layer CKA

outcomes.notes: The claim needs the ReFit-KF sessions, decoded velocities and cursor or robot trajectories, which are not in the dandiset. The dandiset holds one NWB file for B1 only, 9737 trials of 100 Hz high-gamma and low-frequency features (L2 normalized per trial) with a target id and a virtual or robot flag; the data check prints its contents.

outcomes.statement: Trajectories to cardinal targets deviate less from the straight line under IBID than under the ReFit-KF.
outcomes.source: Figure S7I legend; Results, PnP control of a virtual robotic arm, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Results revealed greater median error in trajectories when using ReFit-KF after closed-loop decoder adaptation as compared to IBID after closed-loop decoder adaptation (Mann Whitney U test, z = 6.967 , p = 3.2442 × 10 - 12 )
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the ReFit-KF sessions, decoded velocities and cursor or robot trajectories, which are not in the dandiset. The dandiset holds one NWB file for B1 only, 9737 trials of 100 Hz high-gamma and low-frequency features (L2 normalized per trial) with a target id and a virtual or robot flag; the data check prints its contents.

outcomes.statement: For right thumb OL trials in B1, the mean high-gamma map is preserved across three days (average pairwise r = 0.88), but channel-level high-gamma means over M1/S1 differ between days.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 1; Figure 4A-B
outcomes.quote: Even with a preserved neural map and somatotopy (average pairwise r = 0.88 ), there was little distributional overlap between days ( Fig. 4B , permutation t – tests show significant differences in γ H mean over trials, Day 1 vs. Day 4, t ( 11 ) = 17.87 , p = 1 × 10 – 4
outcomes.notes: The high-gamma features of B1's trials are in the dandiset, but no trial has a day label, the target ids have no names, and there is no electrodes table to locate M1/S1 channels, so right thumb trials of three days cannot be selected. The features are also L2 normalized per trial, unlike the paper's band power.

outcomes.statement: The recording day can be decoded from held-out OL samples on a common multi-day manifold (90.96% in B1, chance 10%; 98.4% in B3, chance 9.09%).
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 1; Figure 4C-D
outcomes.quote: In general, the recording day could be classified from held-out samples on the common manifold ( Fig. 4C – D B1: cross-validated decoding accuracy of 90.96% [90.68% - 91.24%], chance = 10%, B3: cross-validated decoding accuracy of 98.4% [98.24% - 98.54%], chance = 9.09%)
outcomes.notes: The claim needs B1 and B3. Participant B3 is not in the dandiset. For B1 the trials have no day label (metadata_insufficient), and the claim needs the 200 ms delta, beta and high-gamma band-power features of the MLP pipeline (Methods, Spatial feature extraction), which the dandiset does not hold; its features are the biLSTM input (Methods, Spatiotemporal feature extraction for RNNs).

outcomes.statement: After mean-centering each day's data, the recording day can no longer be decoded (B1 10.03%, B3 8.77%, not different from chance).
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 1; Figure 4C-D
outcomes.quote: In contrast, centering and demeaning each day’ data before building a common manifold eliminated discernibility ( Fig. 4C , B1 decoding accuracy: 10.03% [9.71% - 10.37%], chance = 10%, WSR: p = 0.282 , Fig. 4D : decoding accuracy of 8.77% [8.617% - 9.138%], chance = 9.09%, WSR: p = 0.3 )
outcomes.notes: The claim needs B1 and B3. Participant B3 is not in the dandiset. For B1 the trials have no day label (metadata_insufficient), and the claim needs the 200 ms delta, beta and high-gamma band-power features of the MLP pipeline (Methods, Spatial feature extraction), which the dandiset does not hold; its features are the biLSTM input (Methods, Spatiotemporal feature extraction for RNNs).

outcomes.statement: A two-layer MLP on the full feature space also decodes the recording day from held-out trials, significantly above chance in both participants.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 1; Figure S8A-B
outcomes.quote: A MLP in high-dimensional channel-feature space revealed similar significant trial-level decoding accuracies ( Fig. S8A – B )
outcomes.notes: The claim needs B1 and B3. Participant B3 is not in the dandiset. For B1 the trials have no day label (metadata_insufficient), and the claim needs the 200 ms delta, beta and high-gamma band-power features of the MLP pipeline (Methods, Spatial feature extraction), which the dandiset does not hold; its features are the biLSTM input (Methods, Spatiotemporal feature extraction for RNNs).

outcomes.statement: Distances between actions on held-out days increase linearly with the number of prior days used to build the common manifold, in both participants.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 2; Figure 4F-G
outcomes.quote: we found that the pairwise distances between actions on a given day linearly increased as a function of the number of prior days used to build the common manifold (robust linear regression on median Mahalanobis distances, B1: slope b = 0.258 , z = 6.474 , p = 1.847 × 10 – 10 , Fig. 4F
outcomes.notes: The claim needs B1 and B3 OL data by day. Participant B3 is not in the dandiset. For B1 no trial has a day label.

outcomes.statement: In B1, a boundary between two hand actions trained on more prior days generalizes better to a new day, with decoding accuracy rising by 5.5 points per added day.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 2; Figure 4I
outcomes.quote: in B1 trends in decoding performance assessed via linear regression, slope, b = 5.541 ± 0.966 , t ( 8 ) = 5.735 , p = 4.365 × 10 – 4
outcomes.notes: The claim needs B1 OL trials of the 10 daily sessions and a later held-out day; no trial has a day label and the target ids have no names (metadata_insufficient). The claim also needs the 200 ms delta, beta and high-gamma band-power features of the MLP pipeline (Methods, Spatial feature extraction), which the dandiset does not hold; its features are the biLSTM input (Methods, Spatiotemporal feature extraction for RNNs).

outcomes.statement: In B1's first PnP experiment (fixed MLP, 28 days) the average accuracy was 87.43%, time to target 1.195 s and bit rate 1.72 bps.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 3; Figure 5A-C
outcomes.quote: The average accuracy across the entire PnP period was 87.43% [84.0%–90.8%] and the average time to target was 1.195 s [1.087s – 1.33s] ( Fig. 5A – B ). This resulted in a mean bitrate of 1.72 bps [1.51 – 1.94]
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the online decoder outputs, mode-filter outputs, times to target and block structure of the PnP experiments, none of which is in the dandiset. No trial carries a day, session, block, or open-loop or closed-loop label (trial start and stop times are placeholders).

outcomes.statement: In B1's second PnP experiment (38 days, decoder updated with the first experiment's data) the average accuracy was 80.71%, time to target 0.875 s and bit rate 1.848 bps.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 3; Figure 5D-F
outcomes.quote: The average accuracy was 80.71% [77.6% – 83.5%] and the average time to target was 0.875 s [0.842 s – 0.917 s ] resulting in an effective mean bit rate of 1.848 bps [1.68 – 2.02]
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the online decoder outputs, mode-filter outputs, times to target and block structure of the PnP experiments, none of which is in the dandiset. No trial carries a day, session, block, or open-loop or closed-loop label (trial start and stop times are placeholders).

outcomes.statement: Bit rates do not differ between B1's two PnP experiments.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: There were no significant differences in performance between the two PnP experiments (Mann-Whitney U test on bitrates z = – 0.9574 , p = 0.338 )
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the online decoder outputs, mode-filter outputs, times to target and block structure of the PnP experiments, none of which is in the dandiset. No trial carries a day, session, block, or open-loop or closed-loop label (trial start and stop times are placeholders).

outcomes.statement: Daily median PnP accuracy shows no linear trend across days in either B1 experiment or in B3.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 3; Figure S8C-E
outcomes.quote: a linear fit to the daily median revealed stable performance across-days for both ( Fig. S8C – D , p = 0.897 for PnP Exp 1 and p = 0.11 for PnP Exp 2)
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the online decoder outputs, mode-filter outputs, times to target and block structure of the PnP experiments, none of which is in the dandiset. No trial carries a day, session, block, or open-loop or closed-loop label (trial start and stop times are placeholders).

outcomes.statement: Over both B1 PnP experiments the mean effective bit rate was 1.8 bps, with a maximum of 3.351 bps.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Across both experiments, the mean effective bit rate was 1.8 bps [1.66 – 1.93] and the highest was 3.351 bps
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the online decoder outputs, mode-filter outputs, times to target and block structure of the PnP experiments, none of which is in the dandiset. No trial carries a day, session, block, or open-loop or closed-loop label (trial start and stop times are placeholders).

outcomes.statement: In B3's PnP experiment (39 days) the average accuracy was 84.9%, time to target 0.818 s and bit rate 2.22 bps (maximum 3.508 bps), and accuracy stayed stable across days.
outcomes.source: Results, Plug-and-play control in presence of distributional drift, paragraph 4; Figure 5G-I
outcomes.quote: The average accuracy was 84.9% [82.14% – 87.43%], and the average time to target was 0.818 s [0.789 s – 0.848 s ] with a mean bit rate of 2.22 bps [2.046 bps – 2.394 bps ] (maximum of 3.508 bps )
outcomes.notes: Participant B3 is not in the dandiset. The online PnP outputs are not in the dandiset either.

outcomes.statement: Under IBID, the angular error between integrated and ideal diagonal velocities is centred on zero (mean 1.885 degrees, not different from zero), showing integrated off-axis control.
outcomes.source: Results, PnP control of a virtual robotic arm, paragraph 3; Figure 6G
outcomes.quote: The mean of this circular distribution was 1.885 degrees [95% C.I. −1.44 degrees to 5.206 degrees] and not significantly different from zero (circular median, p = 0.348 )
outcomes.notes: The claim needs IBID decoded velocities to diagonal targets, which are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: PCA of velocities during diagonal reaches shows covariation between X and Y velocity, unlike the non-integrated null model whose components recapitulate the cardinal axes.
outcomes.source: Results, PnP control of a virtual robotic arm, paragraph 3; Figure 6F-G
outcomes.quote: In contrast, data revealed significant velocity covariation due to the integration in IBID ( Fig. 6G , left, middle)
outcomes.notes: The claim needs IBID decoded velocities to diagonal targets, which are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: B1 used the PnP decoder proficiently under changed visual perspectives, with 86% (allocentric) and 94% (left-handed) accuracy over 42 trials each.
outcomes.source: Results, PnP control of a virtual robotic arm, paragraph 4; Figure S8H-I
outcomes.quote: We found that B1 could immediately and proficiently use the decoder even with significant visual perturbations, with 86% and 94% decoding accuracies when operating the PnP decoder from either an allocentric or left-handed reference frame respectively (42 trials each
outcomes.notes: The claim needs the online decodes of the perspective perturbation trials, which are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Imagined coactivations of two actions are discernible from the single actions.
outcomes.source: Results, PnP control of a virtual robotic arm, paragraph 3; Figure S8G
outcomes.quote: B1 was also able to access off-axis directions by coactivating multiple representations simultaneously
outcomes.notes: The claim needs trials of imagined coactivations; the dandiset's target ids are 1 to 9 without names, and no trial is labelled as a coactivation.

outcomes.statement: B1 reached 100% accuracy with the mode switch in the virtual reach-to-grasp and transport task after about one week of practice, with a median completion time of 45 s.
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible control of reaching and grasping, paragraph 2; Figure 7D-E
outcomes.quote: B1 gained rapid proficiency in using the mode-switch with 100% accuracy after ~1 week of practice ( Fig. 7D – E , median task completion time of 45s)
outcomes.notes: The claim needs task outcomes and completion times of the mode-switch or Kinova Jaco tasks, by day, which are not in the dandiset. The 1886 robot trials hold neural features and a target id only.

outcomes.statement: With the fixed RNN, B1 completed the real-world reach and rotate task with a median success rate of 90% and completion times of 60.8 s.
outcomes.source: Results, Long-term control of grasping and object manipulation using the Kinova Jaco robot, paragraph 1; Figure 7I-J
outcomes.quote: The median success rate was 90% with task completion times of 60.8 s [54.76 s – 76.95 s ]
outcomes.notes: The claim needs task outcomes and completion times of the mode-switch or Kinova Jaco tasks, by day, which are not in the dandiset. The 1886 robot trials hold neural features and a target id only.

outcomes.statement: In the wall task, B1 reached and grasped the object off the wall proficiently across the whole PnP window (median success 100%, mean 94.6%, median time 38.053 s).
outcomes.source: Results, Long-term control of grasping and object manipulation using the Kinova Jaco robot, paragraph 1; Figure 7K top
outcomes.quote: B1 was able to perform the first part (reach and grasp the target off the wall center) proficiently across the entire PnP testing window and for all levels of approach difficulty ( Fig. 7K top, median success rate of 100%, mean of 94.6%, median time to reach and grasp object 38.053 s [26.825 s – 45.458 s ])
outcomes.notes: The claim needs task outcomes and completion times of the mode-switch or Kinova Jaco tasks, by day, which are not in the dandiset. The 1886 robot trials hold neural features and a target id only.

outcomes.statement: Full wall-task success declined after PnP day 35 (median 88.19% over the first 35 days against 69.05% over days 35 to 210), with longer completion times.
outcomes.source: Results, Long-term control of grasping and object manipulation using the Kinova Jaco robot, paragraph 1; Figure 7K bottom, 7L
outcomes.quote: Here, we observed a drop in performance after PnP day 35 (first 35 days median accuracy of 88.19%, total task completion time 75.52 s [70.22 s – 85.326 s ]; days 35–210 median accuracy of 69.05%, total task completion time 104.854 s [94.648 s – 126.639 s ])
outcomes.notes: The claim needs task outcomes and completion times of the mode-switch or Kinova Jaco tasks, by day, which are not in the dandiset. The 1886 robot trials hold neural features and a target id only.

outcomes.statement: Recalibrating the RNN with about 8 min of data immediately restored full wall-task success to 100%, with a median completion time of 80.73 s.
outcomes.source: Results, Long-term control of grasping and object manipulation using the Kinova Jaco robot, paragraph 2; Figure 7K-L
outcomes.quote: Notably, recalibration of the RNN (data required for decoder update was ~8 min, Methods ), immediately improved the success rate to 100% with a median completion time of 80.73 s [51.277 s – 108.247 s ]
outcomes.notes: The claim needs task outcomes and completion times of the mode-switch or Kinova Jaco tasks, by day, which are not in the dandiset. The 1886 robot trials hold neural features and a target id only.

outcomes.statement: The biLSTM decoder was trained on about 14 hours and 48 minutes of open-loop and closed-loop data from B1's virtual and real-world hDoF experiments, before augmentation and segmentation.
outcomes.source: Methods, RNN decoders based on spatiotemporal activity patterns, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: By the point we got to training a LSTM, we had already collected roughly 14 hours and 48 minutes of experimental open-loop and closed-loop data (prior to data augmentation and segmentation) in the virtual 3D environment and with practice with the Kinova Jaco in the real-world using the MLP
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the whole stored trial, the 9737 trials last 837.4 min (13 h 57.4 min), within 888 +/- 88.8 min; without target ids 8 and 9 they last 814.3 min, also within. The 7851 virtual trials last 540.0 min and the 1886 robot trials 297.3 min; without the robot trials the total is outside the tolerance. Trials last 1.80 to 11.09 s (virtual median 3.41 s, robot median 9.01 s). In trial-id order all virtual trials come first (ids 1 to 7851) and all robot trials after (7852 to 9737); the file does not say whether ids follow the recording order, so this does not show whether the robot trials are later fine-tuning data. Reading (b), the active portion, cannot be run as the file has no task states; it is at most reading (a). The channel-mean high gamma of the virtual trials stays at 0.830 to 0.843 (trial RMS 1) for the first 0.4 s and rises to 0.926 by 0.7 s, while the robot trials show no rise. This low start may be a period before the cue or the reaction time after it, which would lie inside the active (cue and control) portion; the outputs cannot tell which. In the worst case, if the first 0.5 s of every virtual trial were outside the active portion, reading (b) would be 771.9 min, outside the tolerance; this is a lower bound, not an estimate. The criterion asks for a match under one reading, which (a) gives. Whether the robot trials are the real-world practice with the MLP that the paper counts, or the later RNN fine-tuning data, and whether the stored trials are whole trials, is a question for the paper's authors; whether the criterion should require the readings to agree is asked of a reader in questions/001535.yaml.
deviations: Assumed that the dandiset's 9737 trials are the RNN training data the paper counts, including the 1886 robot trials as the real-world practice with the Kinova Jaco (Methods, RNN decoders based on spatiotemporal activity patterns, paragraph 2, "in the virtual 3D environment and with practice with the Kinova Jaco in the real-world using the MLP"). The dandiset description calls them training trials for decoders and points to the paper's biLSTM, but does not say they are exactly its training set, and the robot flag does not say which robot data they are.
Duration is the number of samples divided by 100 Hz; the last minus first timestamp gives 835.7 min, also within the tolerance.
Reading (b) of the criterion (active portion only) could not be run; the file has no task states. The notebook bounds it with the high-gamma time course at the start and end of the trials.

outcomes.statement: In B1, 2x2 spatial pooling of the grid makes single-trial high-gamma activity more consistent and improves online decoding in pilot blocks.
outcomes.source: Figure S3C and S3F legend
outcomes.quote: A Mann Whitney U test revealed significant differences in median variance between pooled and unpooled channels ( z = 8.721 , p = 2.748 × 10 - 18 )

statistics.about: block decoding accuracy, pooled against unpooled

outcomes.notes: The file has no electrodes table, so the place of each channel on the 8x16 grid, which the 2x2 pooling needs, is not given. The right thumb trials are there (target 1 under both the Methods' map and the OSF code's names; 1357 trials) and so is the high gamma, but as the biLSTM input at 100 Hz, L2 normalized per trial, not the MLP pipeline's 200 ms band power, and with no session labels where the paper used one session. The online pilot blocks of the accuracy part are not in the dandiset (data_missing). A variant in the notebook bins the stored high gamma in 200 ms bins, applies a 1 s running average and pools 2x2. Pooling lowers the median per-channel variance to 0.499 of the raw value with channels in row-major order (z = 7.05, p = 1.9e-12) and 0.538 in column-major order (z = 7.12), and under all 200 random layouts (ratios 0.457 to 0.533, z 7.40 to 8.05, p < 0.05 in every one), against the paper's z = 8.721. Since random layouts give the same result, the variant shows only that averaging lowers variance and cannot test the claim about the grid.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only participant B1's biLSTM training trials (high-gamma and low-frequency features at 100 Hz). Participant B3, the Figure 1 imagined-movement task, the delta, beta and high-gamma band-power features of the MLP decoders, the online decoder outputs, the ReFit-KF and IBID velocities and the robot task outcomes behind Figures 1 to 7 are not in it; 51 of the paper's 52 findings cannot be tested.

No trial carries a day, session, block, or open-loop or closed-loop label; the trial table's start_time and stop_time are placeholders (the trial id and id plus one, described as DUMMY), and session_start_time is one date for all trials. Trials collected over many days cannot be grouped by day or context.
The target ids 1 to 9 carry no names or directions in the file or the dandiset metadata. The paper's Methods name seven actions and directions, and its OSF code numbers them in two different orders.
The dandiset description speaks of 7 directional targets; the trial table has 9 target ids, with ids 8 and 9 (132 trials each) only in virtual-environment trials.

The 256 features are not described column by column. The data show columns 0 to 127 almost always positive and 128 to 255 signed, which fits high gamma then low frequency, and each block has an L2 norm of 1 per trial, which the units ("arbitrary") do not state. There is no electrodes table, so the channels cannot be placed on the 8x16 grid.

The is_robot flag does not say whether a robot trial is the real-world practice with the MLP decoder or the later fine-tuning data of the RNN. The paper's 14 h 48 min of training data matches the stored total (837.4 min) only if the 1886 robot trials are counted (540.0 min without them). In trial-id order every robot trial follows every virtual trial, and nothing says whether the ids follow the order of recording.

Question for the paper's authors. Are the 9737 trials of the dandiset the data the biLSTM was trained on (the 14 h 48 min of the Methods), and are its robot trials the real-world practice with the MLP counted there, or the later fine-tuning of the RNN? Is each stored trial the whole trial or only its active portion? The virtual trials' high gamma rises only after about 0.4 s, which could be a period before the cue or the reaction time after it; in the worst case, excluding 0.5 s of each virtual trial would bring the total to 771.9 min.
The subject's age is P38Y, where the paper (STAR Methods, Participants) gives B1 as 41 years old; neither says at what date the age applies, so the two may refer to different dates.

entries.name: 001535-natraj-2025
entries.title: Long-term ECoG BCI training trials of participant B1 (Natraj et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Natraj, Seko, Abiri, Miao, Yan, Graham, Tu-Chan, Chang and Ganguly (2025) that can be tested on dandiset 001535, which holds the 9737 trials of high-gamma and low-frequency features that participant B1's biLSTM decoder was trained on. Only the amount of training data can be tested; the other findings need participant B3, the Figure 1 task, the band-power features of the MLP decoders, session and context labels, online decoder outputs or robot kinematics, none of which the dandiset holds.
